articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Meta's AI support bot got socially engineered harder than a Script Kiddie's first phishing attempt, leading to Obama's Instagram getting defaced with Iranian propaganda. When your AI chatbot has the street smarts of a freshly formatted Windows XP machine, maybe reconsider putting it in charge of account recovery.

articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: CISA—the agency literally tasked with securing America's infrastructure—had a contractor yeet AWS GovCloud keys onto GitHub like it was their personal dotfiles repo. Congress is rightfully losing their minds over this spectacular own-goal in operational security.

articles.title: Welcome New EFF Executive Director Nicole Ozer
articles.summary: A CISA contractor turned GitHub into their personal credentials dumping ground, exposing AWS GovCloud keys and internal systems to anyone with basic git clone skills. Peak irony: the cybersecurity agency getting pwned by elementary OPSEC failures.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: License plate readers have evolved from catching speeders to stalking students and investigating noise complaints—because nothing says 'proportionate response' like mass surveillance for minor infractions. EFF caught cops using ALPR databases like their personal Google for constitutional violations.

articles.title: Patch Now: Another Palo Alto Auth Bypass Bug Under Active Exploit
articles.summary: Microsoft threatened legal action against a researcher who published zero-days, because apparently their preferred disclosure timeline is 'never' and their threat model includes 'accountability.' The security community collectively facepalmed so hard it registered on seismographs.

articles.title: Name That Toon: Mark of (Cybersecurity) Progress
articles.summary: Another Palo Alto auth bypass is getting hammered in the wild, proving once again that 'enterprise security' vendors are about as secure as a screen door on a submarine. Two attack waves and counting—patch now, cry later.

articles.title: New York Comptroller’s Trip to Israel Raised Ethical Concerns, State Commission Said
articles.summary: Philadelphia cops are literally tracking 'First Amendment activity' critical of AI data centers, because apparently exercising constitutional rights while questioning surveillance infrastructure is suspicious. The irony is so thick you could mine it for cryptocurrency.

articles.title: Claude celebrates Anthropic's stock market float with blockbuster ... outage
articles.summary: Microsoft backpedaled harder than a fixie rider on a San Francisco hill after threatening zero-day researchers with legal action. The security community's unified 'WTF' response forced Redmond to clarify they're not actually planning to criminalize vulnerability research.

articles.title: Miasma Supply Chain Attack Compromises Red Hat npm Packages with Credential-Stealing Worm
articles.summary: Dashlane got brute-forced and fewer than 20 encrypted vaults were downloaded, which is either impressive defense or terrible marketing depending on your perspective. At least when password managers get breached, the data is supposed to be encrypted—looking at you, every other company ever.

articles.title: (2026.06.02) (various)
articles.summary: The Miasma supply chain attack compromised Red Hat npm packages with a self-propagating credential-stealing worm, because apparently we needed malware that spreads like gossip in a developer Slack channel. Modern software dependencies: where every 'npm install' is Russian roulette with extra steps.
